advice.heading: What should I do?
advice.highDoNotOpen: Do not open the link, reply, or call any number in the message. Delete it.
advice.neverShareCodes: Never share a one-time code (OTP), card number, PIN, CVV or wallet PIN. Banks, wallets and delivery companies never ask for them by SMS, call or WhatsApp.
advice.contactBrand: This looks like an imitation of {{brand}}. If you are worried about your account, contact {{brand}} only through its official app or the phone number printed on your card or on its official website.
advice.highIfAlreadyEntered: If you already entered your details, call your bank straight away on the number on the back of your card to block the card, and change your password.
advice.highReport: Warn your colleagues and family, and report the message to the institution it pretends to be from.
advice.mediumVerifyFirst: Be careful: do not enter passwords, codes or card details on this link until you have checked it.
advice.mediumNoPressure: Check the request yourself by opening the official app or typing the official website address, not by using the link. Real institutions do not threaten to close your account within minutes.
advice.lowNoIndicators: ETIS found no warning signs, but no system catches every new scam. If the message asks for money or codes, check with the sender through a channel you already trust.
advice.allowlistedCheckSource: This is the official domain of a verified Egyptian institution. Make sure you opened it yourself or from the official app, not from an unexpected message.
